---
title: "Screening & mechanism design"
toc: true
---

## What it is
Screening (principal–agent with adverse selection) studies how a principal designs a menu of contracts to induce agents to reveal private information. Mechanism design generalizes this: choose rules to implement outcomes given strategic agents.

## What’s special
- Key constraint: **incentive compatibility** (each type prefers its intended option).
- Participation (individual rationality) often binds for the lowest type.
- Design trades off efficiency vs information rents.

## One example (two-type contract menu)
Agent type $\theta\in\{H,L\}$ (productivity). Principal offers contracts $(w,q)$: wage and required output.

Utility: $u = w - c(q,\theta)$, where $c(q,H) < c(q,L)$ (high type has lower cost).

Principal wants higher $q$ from $H$ but must prevent $H$ from pretending to be $L$.

**Solution sketch.** The optimal menu typically:
- distorts the low-type contract downward (lower $q$) to reduce information rents,
- gives the high type a contract with higher $q$ and positive rent,
- satisfies IC constraints: $H$ prefers $H$-contract; $L$ prefers $L$-contract.
